To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the angiogenic and lung-colonising capacity of weakly metastatic cells can be enhanced by TPA, whereas the angiogenic and tumour metastasising capacity of highly metastatic cells can by decreased by TPA treatment.
the phorbol ester, TPA, induces angiogenesis and increases lung-colonizing capacity of weakly metastatic cells, while it decreases angiogenesis and metastatic capacity of highly metastatic cells.
TPA-treated B-16F1 cells demonstrated enhanced angiogenic and lung-colonising potential, whereas the angiogenic, gelatinolytic and lung-colonisation capacity of BL6 cells was dramatically decreased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the effects of a single dose of a tumor promoting agent on tumor cells.
the effects of TPA on the angiogenic capacity and the lung-colonizing ability of two different metastatic murine melanoma cell lines.
the role of angiogenesis in tumor metastasis and the effects of TPA treatment in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the angiogenic capacity of B16F1 melanoma cells is enhanced in vitro and in vivo by TPA, whereas in BL6 melanoma cells, TPA induces an inhibition of angiogenic and metastasis-promoting capacity.

TPA treatment of both cell lines induces VEGF and bFGF expression, but only the weakly metastatic cells respond with an increase in angiogenesis and metastatic capacity while in the highly metastatic cells the induction of VEGFs is counteracted by an antagonistic factor(s).
in B16F1 TPA enhances angiogenic capacity and metastatic potential, whereas in BL6 TPA inhibits angiogenesis and metastasis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the effects of phorbol ester on angiogenesis and lung-colonising potential of B16F1 melanoma cells are dependent on their metastatic potential and that these cells can be used as a model system to study angiogenesis and lung colonisation.
TPA treatment can increase angiogenic and metastasizing capacity in B16F1 but decrease it in BL6 cells.
TPA treatment can be used as a strategy to increase or reduce the angiogenic capacity of tumor cells in vitro and in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of TPA on angiogenesis and metastasis is cell type-specific.
TPA can induce angiogenesis and metastasis in weakly metastasizing cells, and that it can suppress the angiogenic and lung colonizing capacity in highly metastasizing cells.
TPA treatment of B16F1 and BL6 melanoma cells induces different biological responses.
